adapalene.high_dose_adverse_effects: Dryness, scaling, stinging, and initial retinization flare when layered with leave-on exfoliants.
adapalene.usage_guidance: Use once nightly; buffer with ceramide moisturizer if dryness occurs and apply daily SPF.

alpha_arbutin.high_dose_adverse_effects: Can release trace hydroquinone in strongly acidic/alkaline environments; keep leave-on face products <=2%.
alpha_arbutin.usage_guidance: Pair with daily sunscreen; avoid during pregnancy out of precaution.

azelaic_acid.high_dose_adverse_effects: Transient pruritus, tingling, and dryness at >=10% especially if layered over low-pH AHAs/BHAs.
azelaic_acid.usage_guidance: Generally pregnancy-compatible and rosacea-friendly when introduced gradually on dry skin.

bakuchiol.high_dose_adverse_effects: Mild contact erythema above 1-2% in reactive skin.
bakuchiol.usage_guidance: Well-tolerated AM/PM; patch test botanical extracts on reactive skin.

benzoyl_peroxide.high_dose_adverse_effects: Strong oxidative agent; concentrations >2.5-5% drastically increase erythema, peeling, oxidative stress, and fabric bleaching without added antimicrobial benefit.
benzoyl_peroxide.usage_guidance: Prefer 2.5-4% wash-off or separated AM usage away from PM tretinoin/retinol and L-ascorbic acid.

centella_asiatica.high_dose_adverse_effects: Rare botanical contact allergy in individuals sensitive to Apiaceae plants.
centella_asiatica.usage_guidance: Calming support ingredient well suited for redness-prone routines.

ceramides.high_dose_adverse_effects: Non-irritating physiological lipid compatible with virtually all actives.
ceramides.usage_guidance: Ideal buffer alongside retinoids or exfoliating acids to mitigate barrier damage.

denatured_alcohol.high_dose_adverse_effects: High-percentage solvent alcohol disrupts intercellular lipid bilayers and amplifies penetration and sting of acids and retinoids.
denatured_alcohol.usage_guidance: Avoid stacking multiple high-alcohol toners and sunscreens on dry, rosacea-prone, or retinized skin.

essential_oils.high_dose_adverse_effects: sensitizing oxidized linalool/limonene hydroperoxides; furanocoumarins in cold-pressed citrus oils induce phytophotodermatitis in UV light.
essential_oils.usage_guidance: Avoid in leave-on facial products if you have sensitive skin, rosacea, or fragrance allergy.

fragrance_parfum.high_dose_adverse_effects: Leading cosmetic trigger of allergic contact dermatitis and rosacea flares, compounded when stacked across cleanser, toner, serum, and cream.
fragrance_parfum.usage_guidance: Select fragrance-free formulations for compromised barriers or reactive skin.

glycolic_acid.high_dose_adverse_effects: Smallest-molecular-weight AHA; >=7% free acid penetrates rapidly causing stinging, over-exfoliation, post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation risk, and UV sunburn sensitivity.
glycolic_acid.usage_guidance: Limit leave-on >=7% toners to 1-3 nights weekly; never layer with retinoids on the same night; wear daily SPF 30+.

hyaluronic_acid.high_dose_adverse_effects: Very low-molecular-weight fragments (>2%) may feel tacky or mildly pro-inflammatory on severely broken barriers if unsealed.
hyaluronic_acid.usage_guidance: Barrier-supportive humectant; seal with an occlusive/emollient moisturizer.

hydroquinone.high_dose_adverse_effects: High systemic absorption (~35-45%), irritant contact dermatitis, exogenous ochronosis with prolonged unmonitored use, and temporary dark staining with benzoyl peroxide.
hydroquinone.usage_guidance: Contraindicated in pregnancy; strictly avoid mixing with benzoyl peroxide; requires diligent SPF 50.

kojic_acid.high_dose_adverse_effects: Sensitization and allergic contact dermatitis risk above 1% leave-on concentration.
kojic_acid.usage_guidance: Keep concentration <=1% and wear daily broad-spectrum SPF.

lactic_acid.high_dose_adverse_effects: Low-pH exfoliation stinging, barrier thinning when stacked with other acids, and UV photosensitivity.
lactic_acid.usage_guidance: Apply 2-3 evenings per week and pair with broad-spectrum sunscreen the following morning.

mandelic_acid.high_dose_adverse_effects: Cumulative stratum corneum thinning and dryness if combined with additional AHAs/BHAs.
mandelic_acid.usage_guidance: Gentler larger-molecule AHA, yet still requires daily SPF protection.

matrixyl_peptides.high_dose_adverse_effects: Amide bonds can undergo acid hydrolysis and lose efficacy when directly layered with low-pH AHAs (pH <3.5).
matrixyl_peptides.usage_guidance: Separate from strong low-pH exfoliating acids between AM and PM.

niacinamide.high_dose_adverse_effects: Optimal efficacy occurs at 2-5%; stacking multiple serums/moisturizers reaching >=10% frequently induces niacin-related flushing, follicular irritation, and stinging.
niacinamide.usage_guidance: Check cleanser, toner, serum, and moisturizer totals so cumulative Niacinamide stays near 2-5%.

panthenol.high_dose_adverse_effects: Minimal irritation risk; heavy balms at 5% can feel rich on oily skin.

peptides_copper.high_dose_adverse_effects: Excess copper peptide stacking (>1-2%) can trigger transient laxity/irritation and chelates/oxidizes L-ascorbic acid or hydrolyzes in low-pH direct acids.
peptides_copper.usage_guidance: Do not layer in the same step with direct AHAs/BHAs or pure L-Ascorbic Acid.

pha_gluconolactone.high_dose_adverse_effects: Mild over-exfoliation only if layered atop strong AHAs, BHAs, or retinoids.
pha_gluconolactone.usage_guidance: Humectant gentle exfoliant suitable for sensitive skin when used as the sole acid.

retinaldehyde.high_dose_adverse_effects: Accelerated cell turnover irritation, redness, and UV sensitivity at concentrations >=0.1%.
retinaldehyde.usage_guidance: PM use only; do not stack with other retinoids or low-pH AHAs in the same routine.

retinol.high_dose_adverse_effects: Retinoid dermatitis, erythema, peeling, transepidermal water loss, and heightened UV sensitivity.
retinol.usage_guidance: Apply at night only on dry skin; start 2-3x weekly and pair with broad-spectrum SPF 30+ daily.

salicylic_acid.high_dose_adverse_effects: Lipophilic keratolytic; leave-on concentrations at 2% or multi-product stacking (cleanser + leave-on toner/serum) strip sebaceous lipids, causing tightness, flaking, and barrier compromise.
salicylic_acid.usage_guidance: Avoid stacking multiple Salicylic Acid products in the same routine; avoid high-dose leave-on BHA during pregnancy.

sodium_ascorbyl_phosphate.usage_guidance: Neutral-pH antioxidant alternative for sensitive or rosacea-prone users.

sulfur.high_dose_adverse_effects: Pronounced desiccation, scaling, and barrier irritation at 5-10% when combined with retinoids, benzoyl peroxide, or salicylic acid.
sulfur.usage_guidance: Use as targeted wash-off mask or spot care; avoid layering with harsh keratolytics.

tea_tree_oil.high_dose_adverse_effects: Undiluted or >2% oxidized terpenes readily provoke allergic and irritant contact dermatitis.
tea_tree_oil.usage_guidance: Never apply undiluted essential oil; avoid on rosacea, eczema, or fragrance-allergic skin.

tranexamic_acid.usage_guidance: Pairs well with niacinamide and sunscreen for uneven tone routines.

tretinoin.high_dose_adverse_effects: Severe barrier disruption, chemical irritation, scaling, burning, and photosensitivity.
tretinoin.usage_guidance: Prescription-strength retinoid; avoid combining with exfoliating acids or benzoyl peroxide in the same session.

vitamin_c_l_ascorbic_acid.high_dose_adverse_effects: Formulated at pH 2.5-3.5; concentrations >=15-20% trigger low-pH stinging, flushing in rosacea, and oxidize copper peptides or benzoyl peroxide.
vitamin_c_l_ascorbic_acid.usage_guidance: Best used in AM under sunscreen to boost photoprotection; keep away from benzoyl peroxide and copper peptides.

pairwise_conflicts.mechanism: Compound stratum corneum exfoliation + accelerated retinoid turnover compromises lipid barrier and triggers acute erythema/peeling.
pairwise_conflicts.resolution: Alternate nights (e.g., Glycolic Acid on Monday/Thursday PM, Retinol on Tuesday/Friday PM) rather than layering in the same evening.

pairwise_conflicts.mechanism: Severe barrier stripping, low-pH irritation, and heightened retinoid dermatitis.
pairwise_conflicts.resolution: Do not combine in the same PM routine; pause strong AHAs until skin is fully acclimated, or separate across non-consecutive nights.

pairwise_conflicts.mechanism: Additive keratolytic irritation and transepidermal water loss.
pairwise_conflicts.resolution: Use on alternating evenings with a ceramide moisturizer buffer.

pairwise_conflicts.mechanism: Dual exfoliation and retinoid signaling increases burning and flaking.
Low-pH AHA exfoliation combined with retinol compromises skin barrier integrity.
pairwise_conflicts.resolution: Alternate nights instead of layering in one PM session.

pairwise_conflicts.mechanism: High risk of chemical irritation and barrier breakdown.
pairwise_conflicts.resolution: Avoid same-night layering; reserve AHA for occasional off-nights only if tolerated.

pairwise_conflicts.mechanism: Lipophilic BHA keratolysis strips sebum and increases retinoid penetration and dryness.
pairwise_conflicts.resolution: Use Salicylic Acid in the AM (or alternate nights) and Retinol in the PM.

pairwise_conflicts.mechanism: Severe xerosis, scaling, and stinging from simultaneous BHA + potent retinoid application.
pairwise_conflicts.resolution: Separate strictly into AM wash-off BHA vs. PM tretinoin, or alternate days.

pairwise_conflicts.mechanism: Multi-acid AHA + BHA layering causes excessive corneodesmosome cleavage and chemical over-exfoliation.
pairwise_conflicts.resolution: Choose one leave-on exfoliant per routine rather than stacking separate AHA and BHA products.

pairwise_conflicts.mechanism: Mutual chemical oxidation degrades non-microencapsulated tretinoin potency while amplifying irritation.
pairwise_conflicts.resolution: Apply Benzoyl Peroxide in the AM and Tretinoin strictly in the PM.

pairwise_conflicts.mechanism: Peroxide oxidation degrades retinol stability and compounds barrier dryness.
pairwise_conflicts.resolution: Separate Benzoyl Peroxide to AM and Retinol to PM.

pairwise_conflicts.mechanism: Redox incompatibility: Benzoyl Peroxide rapidly oxidizes L-Ascorbic Acid into inactive dehydroascorbic acid.
pairwise_conflicts.resolution: Use Benzoyl Peroxide as a rinsed cleanser (thoroughly washed off) or alternate days/times.

pairwise_conflicts.mechanism: Co-application causes transient dark brown/orange oxidative staining of the stratum corneum and heightened irritation.
pairwise_conflicts.resolution: Do not layer together; separate AM and PM and wash hands thoroughly.

pairwise_conflicts.mechanism: Copper ions catalyze metal-induced oxidation of L-Ascorbic Acid, diminishing antioxidant activity.
pairwise_conflicts.resolution: Use L-Ascorbic Acid in the AM and Copper Peptides in the PM.

pairwise_conflicts.mechanism: Low pH (<3.5) protonates peptide ligands, destabilizing the copper-tripeptide complex and hydrolyzing peptide bonds.
pairwise_conflicts.resolution: Separate direct acids and Copper Peptides into different routines (AM vs. PM or alternate nights).

pairwise_conflicts.mechanism: Strong low-pH AHAs can hydrolyze signaling polypeptide chains and reduce efficacy.
pairwise_conflicts.resolution: Apply signaling peptides in AM and Glycolic Acid in PM.

pairwise_conflicts.mechanism: pH mismatch (pH ~3.0 L-Ascorbic Acid vs. pH ~5.5-6.0 Retinol) plus dual active irritation when layered back-to-back.
pairwise_conflicts.resolution: Place Vitamin C in the AM routine under SPF and Retinol in the PM routine.

pairwise_conflicts.mechanism: Compounded keratolytic drying causes severe flaking and barrier disruption.
pairwise_conflicts.resolution: Do not combine leave-on Sulfur and Benzoyl Peroxide in the same session.
